newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian volcano spews hot gas, people evacuated.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian volcano spews hot gas, people evacuated.

text.p: Thousands of Indonesian villagers living near Mount Merapi in Central Java were evacuated on Friday as a precaution after the volcano spewed hot gas, a vulcanology official said.

"The volcano spewed hot gases today. Thousands of people living near Merapi have been evacuated because we don't want to take any risks," the official at the vulcanology office in Yogyakarta told Reuters by telephone.
The official, who gave no other details, said people were moved because the hot gas moved towards a number of villages.

A local government official said more than 5,000 people from four villages had been evacuated. He said there were no reports of casualities and the office continued to monitor the volcano, which has been spewing hot lava and ash this week.
The 2,911-metre (9,548-ft) Merapi erupted without warning in November 1994, killing 60 people and displacing more than 2,000 from its fertile slopes, 400 km (250 miles) east of Jakarta.

Vulcanology director Wimpy S. Tjetjep was quoted by the official Antara news agency as saying on Friday that he believed Merapi would not produce a strong explosion despite its present high activity because of the absence of strong tremors.
Tjetjep said vulcanology officials continued to monitor the volcano.

Villagers near Merapi had been told to be ready to evacuate because of the volcano's intensified activity. Residents of Turgo and Tritis villages, which were hit hard by the 1994 eruption, had earlier been asked to stay in a nearby school.
Merapi, Indonesia's most active volcano, recorded its most destructive eruption this century in 1930, when 1,300 people were killed.
